transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Dana Morris (CTO, Monarch Health), Evan Park (ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Security Lead), Tom Becker (Infra)

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time i think we have about 40 minutes today, quick intro - i'm liam carter ae on the healthcare vertical at redwood, with priya our se and marta csm. you guys?
[00:08] Dana: hey yeah dana here, thanks liam. we'll keep this focused, quick background 14 we are building triage/clinical summarization flows that need really low latency for clinician UX.
[00:18] Evan: evan here, ml infra and we own model infra decisions, curious about token/sec and concurrency, and how streaming will behave for our 8k-ish prompts.
[00:27] Sofia: hi, sofia security 14 we need SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, SSO.
[00:33] Priya: great, thanks. quick agenda: (1) understand your latency targets and concurrency, (2) discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private for those constraints, (3) token/sec benchmarking plan and streaming behavior, and (4) security/compliance notes. sound good?
[00:43] Dana: yes, let's jump in.

-- Qualification / workload patterns --
[01:05] Liam: Dana, you mentioned clinician UX 14 can you give a representative p95 target and concurrency?
[01:12] Dana: our goal is p95 under 200ms for short prompts (100-300 tokens) for the quick triage path; for long summarization (4k-8k tokens) p95 can be 2s or so but we'd like to keep it as low as possible. concurrency peaks are about 40-60 concurrent active clinicians at peak times, sustained about 10-15.
[01:35] Tom: plus we have a batch job that runs nightly for summarization where throughput matters more than latency.
[01:42] Priya: good, that helps. are you currently using any managed LLM API or self-host?
[01:48] Evan: right now prototypes on OpenAI for experiments but moving to a production setup 14 we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated GPUs vs private VPC because of PHI concerns.
[01:58] Liam: totally; typical tradeoff: hosted <-> fastest onboarding, dedicated -> predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, private -> full network isolation / compliance.

-- Latency specifics, streaming and token/sec --
[02:20] Priya: to understand p95 200ms for 100-300 tokens: are those fully generated responses or are you streaming partial tokens back to the UI?
[02:29] Dana: we stream partial tokens 14 clinicians should start seeing text within ~100ms ideally. p95 on first token delivery is what we care about for perceived latency.
[02:38] Priya: ok that's super helpful. streaming first-byte latency is different from full completion p95. we should measure both: time-to-first-byte and time-to-last-byte. for streaming we optimize kv cache warmups and prefix caching to get first-byte lower.
[02:54] Evan: can you talk about tokens/sec numbers? we've seen big variance depending on quantization and batching.
[03:01] Priya: sure 14 rough ballpark on A100/4k seq models: unbatched single-request generation non-quantized might be X tokens/sec, with q4 and batching you can get higher throughput. (note: some transcribed numbers are noisy) for streaming with small seqs, the p95 often dominated by scheduler latency and network. we typically tune batch window to balance latency vs throughput.
[03:28] Tom: what's typical target for token/sec for our nightly batch? we need to run millions of tokens overnight.
[03:34] Liam: Dedicated clusters give predictable tokens/sec and you can scale horizontally. for budgeting we can provide examples 14 e.g., a 4-GPU dedicated pool can sustain about Y tokens/sec for this model family on our internal benchmarks (we'll send exact numbers in the benchmark sheet).

-- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs --
[04:10] Dana: PHI means we might need private or at least VPC with customer-managed keys. what differences in latency do customers see when going from hosted to dedicated?
[04:20] Priya: hosted is multi-tenant but we've optimized for p95; dedicated isolates GPU pools so you avoid noisy neighbors and get more consistent p95. private adds network hops if on-prem or cross region, but keeps data residency and KMS control. for 100-300 token streaming, we've seen hosted p95 in the 150-250ms range for similar customers; dedicated pushed that to sub-150ms p95 in some configs. but exact depends on model, region, and batch settings.
[04:53] Sofia: on KMS 14 do you support customer-managed keys in hosted?
[04:58] Priya: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for dedicated and private; for hosted we offer bring-your-own-key integrations for certain enterprise tiers 14 we will share the security doc.

-- Benchmarks and experiment plan --
[05:20] Liam: recommended next step is a benchmark: you provide representative prompts and load profile, we run a token/sec and streaming latency test across hosted (if allowed), dedicated config, and private if you want to spin up a private control plane.
[05:31] Evan: we want to measure time-to-first-byte, p95 completion, throughput tokens/sec at 40 concurrency, and how batching affects tail latencies.
[05:38] Priya: good 14 we'll run a matrix: cold vs warm cache, different batch windows, q4 vs int8 where available, and test streaming chunk sizes. we'll also capture CPU/GPU utilization and per-token cost.
[05:51] Liam: we'll send a spreadsheet with the prompts and scripts; ideally you can run one with our SE or we can run it against a sample data set in our staging.

-- Technical deep dive: scheduling, KV cache, batching --
[06:12] Priya: quick technical note: for streaming low-latency first byte, we optimize scheduler preemptions and KV cache persistence; when you have repeated prefixes (clinical notes templates) prefix caching can drop time-to-first-byte dramatically. batching helps throughput but increases per-request latency if you wait too long for batch fill. we can configure micro-batching windows like 5-20ms.
[06:39] Evan: how deterministic is p95 under spikes? we want 99% uptime with minimal tail inflation.
[06:45] Priya: with dedicated pools and conservative autoscale we hit SLOs more consistently; hosted has autoscaling too but noisy neighbor risk remains. we also have fallback policies to lower-capacity cheaper variants to avoid request failures.

-- Security / compliance --
[07:08] Sofia: SOC2 type 2 status? audit logs granularity?
[07:12] Marta: we are SOC2 and have audit log exports that include request-level metadata, model version, and redaction markers. logs can be pushed to customer SIEM and we support S3 retention or syslog.
[07:23] Sofia: and SSO/SAML for RBAC?
[07:26] Priya: yes, SSO (SAML, OIDC), RBAC roles. KMS integration for encryption at rest, and you can choose to store keys in your KMS for private and certain enterprise hosted plans.

-- Pricing and TCO questions --
[07:40] Dana: rough TCO for dedicated vs hosted to hit our throughput targets?
[07:45] Liam: we'll provide a sample TCO calc. hosted is pay-as-you-go but unit cost per token is higher; dedicated has commit/reserved pricing and lower unit cost. private has platform fee plus infra. we'll include examples in the pricing packet.

-- Objections / corner cases --
[08:02] Tom: we have strict egress rules in our data center 14 private on-prem is complex for us. can you support a VPC peering approach?
[08:10] Priya: yes, VPC peering and private link options exist; for on-prem there is an appliance option but that requires more lead time. for VPC we can do customer-managed routing and KMS integration.
[08:22] Evan: any gotchas with long context windows (8k) and streaming? we're worried about memory/KV cache blowup and higher per-token cost.
[08:30] Priya: long contexts increase memory footprint and tokenization cost; we use kv cache-friendly strategies and quantization to keep perf acceptable. we also suggest sharded KV cache for very large concurrent workloads. we'll detail configuration in the benchmark report.

-- Recap and explicit next steps --
[09:00] Liam: recap: Monarch needs p95 ~<200ms for short streaming responses and ~2s for long summaries is acceptable; concurrency peaks 40-60; nightly batch throughput requirement for millions of tokens; security needs SOC2, KMS, SSO and audit logs. action: we'll send benchmark template, security pack, and pricing; schedule a 1-hour benchmark with your infra and we'll run hosted/dedicated comparatives.
[09:25] Dana: sounds good. can you also include an example config that got sub-150ms p95 for a comparable healthcare app?
[09:31] Priya: yes we'll include a case study and config recommendations.
[09:36] Sofia: and please include details about log redaction and retention policies.
[09:40] Marta: we'll follow up with calendar invite options for the benchmark run 14 target week of Mar 9.

-- Closing notes / small transcription artifacts --
[09:48] Liam: awesome thanks everyone 14 we'll be in touch.
[09:52] Evan: thanks liam.
[09:55] (end)
